facets.gloss: A basic sense of your ability to handle tasks, understand requirements, and solve problems.
facets.daily_meaning: High scores will make people more willing to take on complex responsibilities; low scores will make people more likely to need more confirmation and support before starting.
facets.why_it_matters: It determines whether you first feel "I can dismantle it" or "I'm not sure I can hold on" when faced with a request.

facets.gloss: Your need for structure, tidiness, planning, and predictability.
facets.daily_meaning: High scorers will proactively establish lists, rules, and sequences; low scorers are more tolerant of on-the-fly adjustments and loose structures.
facets.why_it_matters: It explains why some people rely on order to regain control, while others lose flexibility in excessive order.

facets.gloss: Do you keep commitments, rules and obligations at the forefront of your decision-making?
facets.daily_meaning: High scores are more likely to place "should be done" seriously; low scores are more likely to be reordered by situational value.
facets.why_it_matters: It affects whether a person is pulled by responsibilities or more easily able to renegotiate commitments from changes in needs.

facets.gloss: Your drive for goals, standards, and upward achievement.
facets.daily_meaning: High scorers will continue to pursue better results; low scorers are more likely to use enough availability as a stopping point.
facets.why_it_matters: It determines whether conscientiousness is driven by results or just maintains basic operations.

facets.gloss: Your ability to move forward without immediate feedback.
facets.daily_meaning: A high score can break tasks into long-term rhythms; a low score is more likely to cause interruptions due to fatigue, boredom, or uncertainty.
facets.why_it_matters: It explains why a person may be stuck in executing a goal despite clearly understanding it.

facets.gloss: Your tendency to evaluate risks, consequences, and steps before taking action.
facets.daily_meaning: Those with high scores are more willing to slow down and think clearly before taking action; those with low scores are more likely to make corrections as they go.
facets.why_it_matters: It affects whether you prioritize error prevention before action, or whether you allow action itself to generate answers.
